name: ca-certificates
description: Common CA certificates: a bundle of Mozilla's trusted root Certificate Authority certificates, extracted and converted to PEM format, used by OpenSSL, curl, and other SSL/TLS applications to verify the authenticity of connections.
install: awk -v dir="$DESTDIR/etc/ssl/certs/mozilla" 'BEGIN{n=0} /-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----/{n++; f=dir"/cert"n".pem"} {if (f) print > f} /-----END CERTIFICATE-----/{close(f); f=""}' cacert.pem
for cert in "$DESTDIR/etc/ssl/certs/mozilla"/*.pem; do hash=$(openssl x509 -noout -hash -in "$cert"); ln -sf "mozilla/$(basename "$cert")" "$DESTDIR/etc/ssl/certs/${hash}.0"; done
strip: find "$DESTDIR$PREFIX" -type f -exec sh -c 'file "$1" | grep -q "ELF" && strip --strip-unneeded "$1"' _ {} \; 2>/dev/null || true
